stories.title: Google DeepMind’s new AI model can control a robot’s entire body
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Google DeepMind has released an updated Gemini Robotics AI model.
The new version enables control over an entire humanoid robot's body, not just the upper body.
This advancement allows for complex, whole-body motions, from feet to fingertips.

stories.title: KindaRails2Shell - Critical RCE in Rails via Active Storage (CVE-2026-66066)
stories.author: ethiack.com via hoistbypetard
bullet_points: A critical Remote Code Execution (RCE) vulnerability (CVE-2026-66066) has been discovered in Ruby on Rails.
The vulnerability specifically affects the Active Storage component of the Rails framework.
This represents a high-severity security flaw requiring immediate attention from Rails users.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million in a funding round.
Ollama currently serves a substantial developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent performance shows up to 90% speed increase according to the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance boost results in faster response times and reduced memory usage for LLMs.
The updated engine also contributes to higher quality outputs from the language models.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The key feature is that these agents can run entirely on a user's local hardware.
It integrates built-in support for Ollama, facilitating local LLM execution.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for performance optimization.
The integration specifically targets Apple Silicon, leveraging Apple's native ML framework.
This represents a significant step toward faster, on-device AI inference on Apple hardware.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed to integrate with existing messaging applications.
Its core feature is connecting these apps to local AI coding agents.
Crucially, all AI processing runs entirely on the user's local device, emphasizing privacy and autonomy.

stories.title: Quantum computers outperform classical ones, with results you can trust
stories.author: John Timmer
bullet_points: Quantum computers are demonstrating performance advantages over classical counterparts.
The article addresses the challenge of verifying quantum results using classical methods.
It explores three distinct methodologies designed to ensure the trustworthiness of quantum computation outcomes.

stories.title: Mythos attack on 3rd-round PQC algorithm candidate puts it out of commission
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: A significant vulnerability was discovered in the HAWK algorithm, a candidate for Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC).
The weakness was exposed by an attack method named Mythos, invalidating years of prior testing.
This development is crucial for the ongoing standardization and security of future cryptographic systems.

stories.title: Can AI agents conduct open-ended AI research? Early evidence from two case studies
stories.author: Arvind Narayanan
bullet_points: The paper addresses the critical, yet under-researched, question of whether AI agents can perform open-ended AI research.
It critiques existing evaluation methods, noting that current tests are either too narrow or rely on unreliable peer review processes.
The authors propose a novel methodology to measure progress toward automating AI Research and Development (R&D).

stories.title: APEX-Accounting
stories.author: Bertie Vidgen
bullet_points: Introduction of APEX-Accounting, a new benchmark designed to test frontier AI models on real-world accounting tasks.
The benchmark assesses complex accounting functions such as account reconciliation, expense accrual, and report generation.
The evaluation set is highly rigorous, comprising 160 tasks across 10 worlds, authored and solved by accounting experts.

stories.title: Can AI agents conduct open-ended AI research? Early evidence from two case studies
stories.author: Arvind Narayanan
bullet_points: The paper addresses the critical, yet unproven, hypothesis that AI agents can autonomously conduct open-ended AI research.
It critiques existing evaluation methods, noting that current tests are either too narrow or rely on unreliable peer review processes.
The authors propose a novel methodology to measure progress toward automating AI Research & Development (R&D).

stories.title: MindForge: Teaching Small Language Models Whole-Life-Cycle Software Engineering via Source-Free Program Synthesis
stories.author: Ahmed E. Hassan
bullet_points: Introduces 'MindForge,' a method to teach small Language Models (LLMs) the entire software engineering lifecycle.
Addresses the major limitation of current coding agents: difficulty in generating complete programs from scratch (currently solving <1% of tasks on ProgramBench).
Overcomes the challenge of lacking scalable training environments for end-to-end, from-scratch software development.

stories.title: APEX-Accounting
stories.author: Bertie Vidgen
bullet_points: Introduction of APEX-Accounting, a new benchmark designed to test frontier models' ability to perform real-world accounting tasks.
The benchmark, developed by Mercor and Ramp, includes 160 tasks across 10 simulated accounting 'worlds' involving various file types (spreadsheets, PDFs).
Tasks cover core accounting functions such as account reconciliation, expense accrual, transaction posting, and report generation, validated by accounting experts.

stories.title: DenseOn with the LateOn: Fully Open Dense and Late-Interaction Models for Multilingual, Long-Context, and Code Search
stories.author: Amélie Chatelain
bullet_points: Introduces DenseOn with LateOn, an open-source framework for training dense and late-interaction retrieval models.
Addresses the reproducibility gap in state-of-the-art retrieval models by providing an open end-to-end training recipe.
Demonstrates cross-lingual transferability by using English supervision to improve multilingual retrieval via 'translate-train'.

stories.title: MindForge: Teaching Small Language Models Whole-Life-Cycle Software Engineering via Source-Free Program Synthesis
stories.author: Ahmed E. Hassan
bullet_points: The paper introduces 'MindForge,' a method to train small language models for full-cycle software engineering.

It addresses the significant gap in current AI capabilities: while models can modify code, generating complete programs from scratch remains extremely difficult (less than 1% success on ProgramBench).
The core innovation tackles the lack of scalable training environments necessary to cover the entire software engineering lifecycle.

stories.title: On-Policy Distillation for LLM Safety: A Routing Approach to Template-Robust Realignment
stories.author: Sheng Wen
bullet_points: Addresses a critical vulnerability in LLM fine-tuning where malicious data can embed harmful behaviors.
Proposes 'On-Policy Distillation' using a routing approach for template-robust safety realignment.
Overcomes limitations of existing safety defenses, such as catastrophic forgetting and reduced effectiveness.

stories.title: Gemini Robotics 2 brings whole body intelligence to robots
stories.author: ai2027
bullet_points: Gemini Robotics 2 introduces whole-body intelligence to robotic systems.
This suggests a significant advancement in general-purpose robotic capabilities.
The development points toward a major step in embodied AI research.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 introduces performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden the range of supported models.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, particularly benefiting Apple silicon users.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing Nemotron 3 Ultra.
The model is specifically designed for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is optimized for supporting long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has expanded its capabilities to integrate with advanced AI features.
The new support includes 'subagents' for more complex, multi-step AI workflows.
Integration with 'web search' enhances the real-time knowledge and utility of Claude Code.

stories.title: LinkedIn actually adds a ‘seems like AI slop’ button
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: LinkedIn is implementing a new feature allowing users to report content as 'Seems like AI slop'.
This update is part of LinkedIn's ongoing effort to reduce the prevalence of low-quality, AI-generated content on the platform.
The introduction of a specific reporting mechanism addresses growing user concerns about AI-generated spam and low-effort posts.

stories.title: Google is working on Chrome updates that don’t require restarts
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Google is developing Chrome updates that eliminate the need for browser restarts.
The feature is part of Google's strategy to make software updates less disruptive.
The underlying technology being invested in is referred to as 'dynamic patching'.

stories.title: New MCP specification addresses the main barrier to enterprise adoption
stories.author: Samuel Axon
bullet_points: A new MCP specification has been released.
This specification aims to overcome a primary hurdle in enterprise adoption.
A new policy for the AI protocol guarantees feature stability and prevents sudden removals.

stories.title: Musk went to “war,” sought jail time for X ad boycotts—but case ends with a whimper
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: Musk initiated legal action against advertisers boycotting X.
The legal battle surrounding the ad boycotts concluded without a major ruling.
Advertisers and X have agreed to reset their business relationship.

stories.title: Who wins and who loses after US bans foreign robots?
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: The US government is considering a ban on foreign-made robots.
The article suggests this ban might negatively impact, rather than benefit, the US robotics industry.
The news touches upon geopolitical trade policy intersecting with advanced robotics technology.

stories.title: Elon Musk’s xAI is trying to sue its way out of a Grok reckoning
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: Elon Musk's xAI is reportedly engaging in legal action regarding Grok.
The core of the legal dispute involves a ban on a 'nudifying app' in Minnesota.
Musk is arguing that the state's ban infringes upon constitutional rights.

stories.title: The Social Cost of an AI Teammate: How an Artificial Teammate Reshapes Human-Human Communication in Small-Team Decision-Making
stories.author: Spencer JaQuay
bullet_points: Investigates how the integration of conversational AI as a 'teammate' alters human-human communication during team decision-making.
Uses a randomized controlled study involving high-stakes moral dilemmas to analyze sociocognitive dynamics.
Employs Group Communication Analysis (GCA) and lexical analysis to study the impact of AI presence on team discourse.

stories.title: Improving Item Discoverability in e-Commerce Search via Related Intent Generation
stories.author: Tejaswi Tenneti
bullet_points: Addresses the limitation of traditional e-commerce search systems that prioritize strict query matching over item discoverability.
Proposes a scalable system using 'intent-conditioned recall expansion' to improve search results.
Focuses on enhancing user satisfaction by surfacing substitute, complementary, and thematically related items, particularly relevant for grocery e-commerce.

stories.title: OmegaUse-OfficeVal: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Long-Horizon Office-Suite Tasks with Economic Grounding
stories.author: Hua Wu
bullet_points: Introduces OmegaUse-OfficeVal, a new benchmark for evaluating LLM agents.
Focuses on long-horizon, real-world office-suite tasks, moving beyond simple task completion.
Adds 'economic grounding' to the evaluation, assessing agent performance relative to cost.

stories.title: Cost-Sensitive Conformal Prediction and Human-in-the-Loop Abstention for Imbalanced High-Stakes Decision Support: A Multi-Domain Benchmark
stories.author: Shyamal Lakhanpal
bullet_points: Addresses a critical limitation in standard Conformal Prediction (CP) when applied to high-stakes, imbalanced datasets.
Demonstrates that standard CP severely under-covers rare, costly minority classes (e.g., fraud, critical medical events).
Proposes a solution involving Cost-Sensitive CP and Human-in-the-Loop Abstention for robust uncertainty quantification.

stories.title: Linguistic Monoculture in LLM-Assisted Language Use
stories.author: Lutz Oettershagen
bullet_points: Widespread use of LLMs for text drafting and revision risks creating 'linguistic monoculture'.
This monoculture suggests that over-reliance on shared LLM models may reduce natural variation in human language.
The research introduces a mathematical framework to model the interaction between authors and LLMs as distributions over linguistic features.

stories.title: Do You Really Need to Pretrain Q-Functions for Online RL Fine-Tuning?
stories.author: Chelsea Fin
bullet_points: Challenges the conventional wisdom that Q-functions must be pre-trained when fine-tuning policies in Reinforcement Learning (RL).
Presents evidence that online RL can achieve high performance and reliability even with a randomly initialized Q-function.
Suggests a potential simplification or change in best practices for value-based RL fine-tuning.

stories.title: Skillful forecasting of offshore winds from satellite scatterometer constellations
stories.author: Angela Meyer
bullet_points: The research addresses the critical need for accurate, short-term (minutes to hours) offshore wind forecasts for power system stability.
Traditional Numerical Weather Prediction (NWP) models are not optimized for the high-frequency initial-condition accuracy required for these short-lead-time forecasts.
The study proposes using satellite scatterometer observations directly for forecasting, moving beyond their current assimilation role in NWP.

stories.title: Cost-Sensitive Conformal Prediction and Human-in-the-Loop Abstention for Imbalanced High-Stakes Decision Support: A Multi-Domain Benchmark
stories.author: Shyamal Lakhanpal
bullet_points: Addresses a critical flaw in standard Conformal Prediction (CP) when applied to high-stakes, imbalanced datasets.
Demonstrates that standard CP severely under-covers rare, costly minority classes (e.g., fraud, critical medical events).
Proposes a solution involving Cost-Sensitive CP and Human-in-the-Loop Abstention for robust uncertainty quantification.

stories.title: Mental World Modeling
stories.author: Yiran Zhao
bullet_points: The paper addresses a limitation in current world models, which only predict physical states (what/where) rather than human behavior.
It proposes 'Mental World Modeling' to incorporate hidden mental states like beliefs, intentions, and social considerations of agents.
The core argument is that ignoring an agent's internal knowledge leads to incorrect predictions of action, even in physically accurate scenes.

stories.title: SpecFirst: Behavioral Specification Elicitation as a First-Class Step in Agent-Based Program Synthesis from Scratch
stories.author: Ahmed E. Hassan
bullet_points: Program synthesis from scratch remains a significant challenge for LLM-based agents, even with advanced models.
Current state-of-the-art benchmarks show frontier models solve less than 1% of instances when starting only from natural language and an oracle.
The proposed 'SpecFirst' framework addresses this by separating behavioral specification elicitation as a distinct, crucial step before code synthesis.

stories.title: OmegaUse-OfficeVal: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Long-Horizon Office-Suite Tasks with Economic Grounding
stories.author: Hua Wu
bullet_points: Introduces OmegaUse-OfficeVal, a new benchmark for evaluating LLM agents.
Focuses on long-horizon office-suite tasks, moving beyond simple conversational tests.
Adds 'economic grounding' to the evaluation, assessing task completion at a reasonable cost.

stories.title: Linguistic Monoculture in LLM-Assisted Language Use
stories.author: Lutz Oettershagen
bullet_points: Widespread reliance on LLMs for text generation and revision may lead to 'linguistic monoculture'.
This phenomenon suggests that shared LLM usage could reduce natural variation in population-level language.
The research proposes a mathematical framework to model the interaction between authors and LLMs as distributions over linguistic features.

stories.title: Data, Context & RAG Lineage Governance for Enterprise AI Agents
stories.author: jitu028
bullet_points: Focuses on advanced governance for Enterprise AI Agents utilizing Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG).
Details specific technical implementations like query-time Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC) and cryptographic lineage.
Addresses critical security concerns such as outbound payload sanitization within agentic systems.

stories.title: How to Test AI Agents Without Calling More LLMs
stories.author: raju_dandigam
bullet_points: Addresses the high cost associated with testing AI agents due to sequential LLM calls.
Proposes methods to evaluate AI agent performance without relying on expensive, chained LLM interactions.
Relevant to developers and researchers building complex, multi-step AI systems.
